findings.problem: PacketWorkflow exposes bool lifecycle flags (is_validated, is_sent) and a status String as public fields. Any combination is constructible — e.g. is_sent=true with is_validated=false, or status='pending' with is_sent=true — making illegal states representable.
findings.failure_mode: A packet can be marked sent without being validated, or have contradictory status/flag pairs. Callers can mutate fields freely without enforcing domain invariants (validated before sent, status must reflect lifecycle).
findings.fix: Replace is_validated and is_sent with a single typed PacketState enum (e.g. Pending, Validated, Sent). Remove status String or make it a derived read-only accessor. Use a private struct with public constructors/factory methods that enforce invariants.

findings.problem: status field is a plain String instead of a typed enum or newtype. Status is a domain concept with lifecycle invariants but is represented as an untyped string.
findings.failure_mode: Any arbitrary string can be assigned to status (e.g. status="deleted" or status=""), violating domain invariants. No compile-time guarantee that status matches the lifecycle state.
findings.fix: Replace String status with a PacketStatus enum (e.g. Pending, Sent). Remove redundant is_sent/is_validated bools. Let status alone track lifecycle.

findings.problem: is_validated and is_sent are separate bool fields encoding lifecycle state. These should be a single enum typestate per the functional-core-performance reference: 'Replace bool lifecycle flags, status strings, and Option lifecycle fields with enums or typestates.'
findings.failure_mode: Two independent bools can diverge (e.g. both true, both false, or is_validated=false/is_sent=true), creating contradictory state that no single boolean can express. No compile-time guarantee of a single coherent lifecycle state.
findings.fix: Replace both bools with a single PacketState enum: enum PacketState { Pending, Validated, Sent }. Remove status String entirely or derive it.

findings.problem: mark_sent accepts any PacketWorkflow regardless of current state. There is no check that the packet was validated before being sent. The function unconditionally sets is_sent=true and status='sent'.
findings.failure_mode: An unvalidated packet can transit directly to sent state, bypassing the validation gate. This is a domain invariant violation — packets must be validated before being sent.
findings.fix: Require the packet to be in a Validated state before transitioning to Sent. Use an enum typestate so this is enforced at the type level, not a runtime check. Change signature to accept only the validated variant.

findings.problem: All struct fields are pub, allowing external code to mutate PacketWorkflow fields arbitrarily without going through any domain methods or constructors.
findings.failure_mode: External code can set is_sent=true, status="whatever", is_validated=false simultaneously, creating impossible states without any domain logic enforcement.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide a public constructor (e.g. PacketWorkflow::new) and state-transition methods (e.g. validate(), send()) that enforce invariants.

findings.problem: id is a plain String. Packet identifiers are a domain concept with rules (e.g. format, uniqueness, non-empty) but have no type-level enforcement.
findings.failure_mode: An empty string, null bytes, or malformed IDs can be assigned. No compile-time distinction between a Packet ID and any other string (e.g. a name or status string).
findings.fix: Define a `PacketId` newtype with a fallible constructor that validates format constraints. Use `PacketId` instead of `String` for the id field.

findings.problem: mark_sent assigns `"sent".to_string()` each time, allocating a new String on the heap. With a typed enum this allocation disappears entirely.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation on every send operation. Combined with the enum typestate fix, the status field and allocation both vanish.
findings.fix: Replace status String with an enum variant `PacketStatus::Sent`. Eliminate the .to_string() call.

findings.problem: mark_sent is a free function that mutates a struct in place rather than a pure function returning a new state, or a method on a typestate-aware type. There is no functional core — logic is just imperative mutation of public fields.
findings.failure_mode: No separation between pure domain logic and imperative shell. The function has no error handling, no state validation, and mutates data directly, making it hard to test deterministically or reason about.
findings.fix: Define mark_sent as a method on the typestate type that returns a Result<PacketWorkflow, DomainError>. Or better: use an enum typestate so the transition is a type-level operation with no runtime mutation.

residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate is structurally unsafe — all fields are public primitives with no typestate enforcement. The core issue (illegal states representable via bool flags + String status) makes every downstream use a potential invariant violation. Fix requires typestate enum + private fields + validated constructors before any other Holzman gates are meaningful.
